item.title: Up to 20,000 unaccounted for after ISIS camp empties in Syria
item.description: U.S. intelligence agencies have concluded that between 15,000 and 20,000 individuals, including affiliates of the Islamic State, are now unaccounted for following a mass departure from Syria's al-Hol detention camp, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal citing U.S. officials familiar with the assessment. The finding underscores what analysts and Western diplomats have described as one of the most acute counterterrorism failures since the fall of ISIS's self-declared caliphate in 2019.

item.title: EU fails to agree on new Russia sanctions package ahead of war anniversary
item.description:
EU ambassadors failed to reach agreement on the bloc's 20th package of sanctions against Russia on Friday, with a proposed ban on maritime services for Russian oil tankers remaining the central obstacle as the fourth anniversary of Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine approaches on February 24.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas expressed confidence the package would still be adopted, telling reporters, "Next Monday, we aim to adopt the 20th sanctions package against Russia". Negotiations among ambassadors are expected to continue over the weekend before foreign ministers meet in Brussels on February 23.

item.title: Trump orders new 10% global tariff hours after Supreme Court strikes down IEEPA levies
item.description:
President Trump appeared in the White House briefing room on Friday afternoon flanked by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Attorney General Pam Bondi, and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer to deliver a defiant response to the Supreme Court's 6-3 ruling that his sweeping tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act were unlawful. Trump called the decision "deeply disappointing" and announced he would immediately sign an executive order imposing a new 10% global tariff under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, "over and above our normal tariffs already being charged".

The announcement marks the administration's first concrete step in a contingency plan developed over months in anticipation of a possible court defeat.

item.title: UK considers removing Andrew from royal succession
item.description:
The UK government is considering legislation to remove Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor from the royal line of succession, the BBC reported on Friday, a day after the former prince became the first senior royal in modern history to be arrested. The move marks a reversal from the government's position in October 2025, when Downing Street said there were "no plans" for legislative changes to the succession order.

Andrew, 66, was arrested at Wood Farm on the King's Sandringham estate on Thursday morning — his birthday — on suspicion of misconduct in public office. Thames Valley Police said he was detained as part of an investigation into allegations that he shared confidential government information with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein while serving as the UK's special trade envoy. He was held for approximately 11 hours at Aylsham police station in Norfolk before being released under investigation.

item.title: NOAA adopts new El Nino index as warming outpaces old system
item.description: The natural El Nino cycle that shapes weather patterns around the globe is both amplifying and being reshaped by a rapidly warming planet, prompting U.S. forecasters to adopt a new measurement system and researchers to trace how the interplay between these forces helped drive recent record temperatures.

item.title: Germany's Merz to visit China for first talks with Xi since taking office
item.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz will depart Berlin on Tuesday for his first official visit to China, where he will meet with President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang in what German officials described as an effort to find "the right balance of cooperation" between Europe's largest economy and its biggest trading partner.

item.title: New studies bolster theory that viruses sparked complex life
item.description: A pair of recent studies is reviving a long-debated question in evolutionary biology: did viruses help give rise to all complex life on Earth? The discovery of a new giant virus in Japan and fresh genomic evidence that ancient microbes could tolerate oxygen are together lending new weight to the idea that the cell nucleus — the defining feature of plants, animals, and fungi — may trace its origins to a viral infection billions of years ago.

item.title: New battery designs tackle fire risk and scarce metals
item.description: A flurry of new studies published this week from laboratories in China, Hong Kong, and the United States detail battery designs built around safer electrolytes and more durable materials, offering a glimpse of energy storage systems that could move beyond the flammability and resource constraints of conventional lithium-ion technology.

item.title: Guterres calls for science-based AI policy at India summit
item.description: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres urged the global community to put science at the center of artificial intelligence governance, warning that "policy cannot be built on guesswork" and calling for evidence-based cooperation to harness AI for sustainable development. His remarks came at a side event on the role of science in international AI governance on February 20, during the final day of the India AI Impact Summit 2026 in New Delhi.

item.title: Russia hits Ukraine with missile, 120 drones overnight, injuring at least 15
item.description:
Russian forces struck civilian targets across Ukraine with a barrage of missiles and drones on the night of February 20, injuring at least 15 people and damaging homes, schools, and energy infrastructure, as peace talks between Kyiv and Moscow remain stalled.

Ukraine's Air Force reported that Russia launched an Iskander-M ballistic missile and approximately 120 drones overnight, with Ukrainian air defenses shooting down or jamming 106 of them. The remaining drones hit 19 locations across the country, causing fires, structural damage, and civilian casualties.

item.title: Cuban security forces withdraw from Venezuela under US pressure
item.description:
Cuban security advisers and medical personnel have been leaving Venezuela in recent weeks, marking a historic unraveling of the decades-old alliance between Caracas and Havana as Washington presses Interim President Delcy Rodríguez to sever ties with the island's communist government.

The withdrawals, first reported by Reuters on Saturday and confirmed by 11 sources familiar with the matter, represent the most concrete sign yet that the political bond holding together Latin America's two most prominent leftist governments is fraying under sustained American pressure.

item.title: Scientists propose mission to chase interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS
item.description:
As interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS barrels toward a close flyby of Jupiter next month, scientists are both racing to study its surprising behavior and drafting plans for a spacecraft that could one day catch up to the alien visitor — even after it leaves the solar system for good.

The comet, only the third interstellar object ever detected, was discovered on July 1, 2025, by the NASA-funded ATLAS telescope in Chile. Since then, a fleet of space- and ground-based observatories has tracked it through the inner solar system. Now, as it heads outward past the orbit of Jupiter, new findings and a mission concept published this month have renewed scientific interest in the fleeting cosmic wanderer.

item.title: France says EU ready to retaliate after Trump raises global tariff to 15%
item.description:
The European Union warned Saturday that it is prepared to strike back at the United States after President Donald Trump moved to reimpose and then escalate global tariffs in rapid succession, raising the prospect of a renewed transatlantic trade war less than 24 hours after the Supreme Court dealt a major blow to his trade agenda.

France's trade minister Nicolas Forissier told the Financial Times that Paris is coordinating with EU counterparts and the European Commission over Trump's decision to impose a blanket tariff on imports. "Should it become necessary, the EU has the appropriate instruments at its disposal," Forissier said. French officials told the newspaper that Brussels is weighing deployment of the anti-coercion instrument, a so-called "trade bazooka" that could restrict US technology companies from EU public procurement, impose export controls, or levy charges on services. A suspended package of retaliatory tariffs covering more than €90 billion in US goods could also be reactivated.

item.title: Greenland's ice sheet is churning like Earth's mantle, study finds
item.description:
Giant plume-like structures deep inside the Greenland ice sheet, a mystery that has puzzled researchers for more than a decade, are likely caused by thermal convection — the same slow, churning process that moves molten rock in Earth's mantle, according to a study published this month in The Cryosphere.

The finding, led by researchers at the University of Bergen in Norway alongside scientists from NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center and the University of Oxford, challenges the long-held view of ice sheets as rigid, static masses and could reshape how scientists model future sea level rise.

item.title: Two studies reveal Greenland ice is softer and melting faster than expected
item.description: Two new studies published this month have reshaped scientists' understanding of the Greenland ice sheet, revealing that it harbors slow, convection-like churning deep beneath its surface and that extreme melting events have intensified at an unprecedented pace since 1990. Together, the findings underscore how climate change is transforming the world's second-largest ice mass in ways researchers did not anticipate.

item.title: India postpones U.S. trade trip after Supreme Court strikes down Trump tariffs
item.description:
India has postponed a key trade delegation to Washington that was set to finalize an interim bilateral trade deal, after the U.S. Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump's sweeping tariff regime and the White House scrambled to replace it with new levies under an untested legal authority.

The Indian negotiating team, led by chief negotiator Darpan Jain, had been scheduled to begin a three-day meeting in Washington on February 23 to convert a framework agreement into a binding legal pact, according to Reuters. Both governments agreed the visit should be rescheduled after they assess the fallout from Friday's court ruling and Trump's rapid imposition of replacement tariffs.

"The visit of the Indian chief negotiator and delegation will be scheduled later at a mutually convenient date once both governments complete internal assessments," a source familiar with the matter told CNBC. A new date has not been set, though sources indicated to India Today that the delay is expected to last weeks rather than months.

item.title: HKU engineers find physics principle that breaks sound absorption limits
item.description: Engineers at the University of Hong Kong have identified a physics principle that redefines the limits of noise reduction in ventilated spaces, offering a potential path toward quieter buildings, vehicles, and industrial environments without sacrificing airflow.

item.title: Trump says US will send hospital ship to Greenland
item.description:
President Donald Trump declared Saturday that the United States would send a "great hospital boat" to Greenland, claiming residents of the Arctic territory are "sick and not being taken care of." Denmark swiftly dismissed the plan, with the defense minister stating the self-governing territory's population already receives adequate healthcare.

Trump's announcement, made on Truth Social alongside an image of the USNS Mercy, a 1,000-bed naval hospital ship, came on the same day Danish military forces evacuated a crew member from a U.S. submarine off the coast of Greenland's capital, Nuuk, for urgent medical treatment. The timing raised questions about whether the submarine incident prompted the president's post.

item.title: Mexican army kills 'El Mencho,' leader of Jalisco cartel
item.description:
The Mexican army killed Nemesio Rubén Oseguera Cervantes, the elusive leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel known as "El Mencho," during a military operation on Sunday in the western state of Jalisco, a federal official told the Associated Press. The death of one of the world's most wanted drug lords triggered a violent response from the cartel, with burning vehicles and roadblocks erupting across at least six Mexican states.

The operation, carried out by special forces of the Mexican army and National Guard, took place in the mountainous area near Tapalpa in southern Jalisco, according to multiple Mexican media reports citing federal sources. El Mencho had long been reported to suffer from chronic kidney failure, which limited his mobility and forced him to rely on clandestine medical care in rural communities of Jalisco.

item.title: Oman confirms US-Iran nuclear talks set for Thursday in Geneva
item.description:
The United States and Iran are preparing for a third round of indirect nuclear negotiations in Geneva this week, as both sides signal a willingness to keep talking even as President Donald Trump weighs military action against Tehran.

Oman's Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi confirmed on Sunday that the talks are scheduled for Thursday, describing the upcoming session as proceeding "with a positive push to go the extra mile towards finalising the deal." Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, appearing on CBS News' "Face the Nation" the same day, said he expects to meet US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff in Geneva on Thursday, adding, "I believe that still, there is a good chance to have a diplomatic solution which is based on a win-win game."
